newsitem.title: UK: Falklands awards oil licenses, Argentine bid fails.
newsitem.headline: Falklands awards oil licenses, Argentine bid fails.

text.p: The Falkland Islands government on Monday said it would issue licenses to 13 companies to explore for oil in waters to the north of the British territory.
Chief Executive of the Falklands Islands government Andrew Gurr said a joint application from British Gas and Argentina's Yacimientos Petroliferos Fiscales (YPF) was the only bid that failed.
"That was the only consortium that got nothing but that was partly because they limited their bidding to the two most successful tranches," Gurr told Reuters.
But Gurr said the next licensing round would "almost certainly" cover an area of special cooperation which straddles the median line between the Islands and the Argentinian mainland.
Seven tranches were awarded, equal to about 48 North Sea blocks, and covering an area of roughly 12,800 square kilometres.

The seven consortium are as follows: Tranche A will be operated by Amerada Hess, Fina Exploration, Murphy South Atlantic, Teikoku Oil and Argos Evergreen Ltd and Tranche B by Shell Exploration with Agip as partner.
Tranche C&D will be operated by LASMO and include Clyde Expro and newly formed Falklands oil company desire Petroleum.
Tranche F will operated by International Petroleum Corporation with Sands Petroleum.
Tranches I&L were awarded to Desire Petroleum.
Seismic surveying is expected to begin in January 1997 and drilling could start as soon as October or November next year.
Gurr said he regretted the failure of the British-Argentine bid, adding that the licences were awarded purely on a commercial basis.

"It was really to do with their own judgement of risk on the tranches that were on offer and their own commitment, which was not as significant as the others who actually won those tranches," he said.
The economy of the islands will receive a boost from collection of the licence fees and development of service industries to support the exploration activity offshore.
"Licences have been awarded which will give rise to a large and varied work programme covering much of the North Falkland Basin," said oil licensing administrator John Martin.
"The combined committed work programme will ensure a vigorous entry of the Falkland Islands into the oil exploration industry," he added.
Earlier this year, Argentina and Britain announced that they had set up a joint committee to administer hydrocarbon exploration in waters around the disputed islands.
The two countries fought a 10-week war over the Falklands in 1982. About 1,000 servicemen on both sides died as a British task force dislodged Argentine troops who briefly occupied the islands.
Buenos Aires still claims sovereignty over the islands.
